label: thm:terms:dilemma (iii)-(v); cor:terms:table rows 3-4; prop:terms:a1fit; thm:terms:binary (i),(ii),(iv); prop:terms:ontology (a); cor:terms:freededuction; prose of sec:terms:craig, sec:terms:ontology
problem: The fit-class results for finite and observational theories are stated for the section's general background B. def:terms:obs says B may contain theoretical symbols, def:terms:literal and app:terms assume only the literal setting, and 'consistent'/'proves' include B. But every proof builds a model without B ((T,C^T,R) or U), and the record states B=empty (terms Cor 5.4, section 6). With admissible nonempty B the statements fail. (1) B1={forall z not s1s1z=z}: theta_2 becomes vacuous, so T^O_V and A^O_M with B1 prove R(t_w) and not R(t_w); this breaks the consistency claims of thm:terms:binary(ii) and prop:terms:a1fit and the observational half of (iii)/(iv). (2) B2 = the R-free part of T^C_V plus definitions of P1,P2 from C: T={forall x(P1x->Rx), forall x(P2x->not Rx)} is finite, unary and compatible with ThT, yet with B2 it proves exactly the literals of any decidable X and proves no false {e,s0,s1}-sentence; this refutes (iv) and prop:terms:ontology(a) as worded. (3) B4={exists z s1s1z=z} with T''={(exists z s1s1z=z)->phi : phi in T^O_V} refutes (iv) even with symbol-disjoint B.
fix: State B = empty (as cor:terms:ontology already does) in thm:terms:dilemma (iii)-(v), cor:terms:table rows 3-4, prop:terms:a1fit, thm:terms:binary, cor:terms:freededuction and the prose of sections 8.2-8.4. In prop:terms:ontology(a) write 'T proves' (plain derivability) or assume B=empty. Alternatively state the sufficient conditions: B true in the model used and free of the hypothesis's symbols for the constructions, and B a subset of ThT in {e,s0,s1} for (iv) and ontology(a).

label: sec:terms:finite (sentence introducing prop:terms:ramsey), l.99
problem: The main text says 'no finite first-order theory without a function symbol has the same consequences' as {Inf_m}. This is false: in {=,<} the finite theory 'irreflexive, transitive, no maximum' has only infinite models and the model (N,<), so its {=}-consequences are those of {Inf_m}. The record (terms Prop 7.1(c)) and app-terms prop:terms:ramsey(c) say only 'in {=}, nor in any monadic extension'. The claim also contradicts the section's thesis that polyadic relations pay.
fix: Replace with 'no finite first-order theory in pure equality, or with unary predicates added, has the same consequences'. Optionally note that a binary relation (a strict order without maximum) also gives a finite theory.

label: sec:terms:finite, l.99
problem: 'Kpad(n) ... tends to infinity, though more slowly than every computable unbounded function' is false without 'nondecreasing': a computable unbounded function that is 0 on odd n is not eventually above Kpad. Record terms Thm 6.2(b) and app thm:terms:infinity(b) say 'nondecreasing'; logic.tex already does.

label: thm:terms:dilemma (proof, clause (iii))

Part (iii) rests on (F1), APSPACE=EXPTIME (via prop:terms:a1fit and the (a1) part of thm:terms:binary), the one-tape simulation (lem:terms:twostack) and the earlier report's Props E.21, E.23. The record's status: '(iii) proved under (F1), given SD Thm 3.1, Prop 4.3, Cor 4.4, the one-tape simulation and CKS'.
fix: Append 'under ass:soi:F1, given the one-tape simulation and APSPACE = EXPTIME' to the (iii) clause.

label: sec:terms:craig, l.81 (description of thm:terms:binary)
problem: 'derivations whose length and line size are linear in the time and space of a one-tape simulation of V plus the input length' drops the certificate length. N_run = O(T_1+|x|+|z|), line size O(l+1) with l = O(S_1+|x|+|z|) (record Lemma 4.5(iii), Thm 4.6(iii)).
fix: Write 'plus the lengths of the input and the certificate'.

label: sec:terms:craig, l.81 (definition of theta_2)
problem: The main text defines theta_2 with bound variable y, not marked fresh, and reuses y in Std(y). The record corrected exactly this capture problem (terms section 4.2, section 11 item 14, referee B2); app-terms uses y_theta and states freshness.

label: paragraph after thm:terms:everyregular
problem: 'checks the theories of five regular languages on all data with |w|<=9' overstates coverage: two languages (t4_regular) on all 1023 data |w|<=9, and three (rb4) on all 511 data |w|<=8.
fix: Write 'two regular languages on all data with |w|<=9 and three more, independently, with |w|<=8'.

label: sec:logic:pi1, paragraph after thm:logic:threshold, l.87
problem: One paragraph uses 'prior probability of being proved' for Unif(O_pi) and 'prior probability of provability' for Bel_0(pi), the defined term, which equals Unif(O_pi)-Inc_0. Reading the second as Unif(O_pi) makes the T_k claim false when 2^-k <= Inc_0.
fix: Write 'every Pi1* sentence pi with Unif(O_pi) above a uniformly random level' and 'with Bel_0(pi) >= 2^-k'.

label: text after thm:logic:arith, l.68
problem: 'the diagonal reports a different, unrefuted ticket' is right only when B∪W_k is consistent and proves Lot^ar_k; otherwise j*_k is just the least j != j°_k and may be refuted. Also 'the least ticket that W_k refutes' should be 'that B∪W_k refutes'.
fix: Write: 'the true winner of lottery k is the least ticket that B∪W_k refutes (0 if none); the diagonal reports as the loser a different ticket, one that B∪W_k does not refute whenever B∪W_k is consistent and proves Lot^ar_k, and that report is true.'

label: sec:logic:lottery, paragraph 'Relatives', l.56
problem: 'the modified Demski prior ... too gives the lottery stream positive probability' is stated outright. The record has '[proved, for the process as described]', the bib report (section 3, item 7) says the post's definition was not read, and app-logic keeps the qualifier.
fix: Add 'for the process as described in those works' (and cite app:logic:lottery).

label: sec:logic:lottery, paragraph 'Relatives', l.56
problem: 'randomised learners can succeed where deterministic ones cannot' omits the threshold qualifier that the bib report's suggested sentence kept: above a success-probability threshold a probabilistic learner can be derandomised (Pitt). The lottery's survival probability 0.2888 is below 1/2, consistent with this.
